name: cavemio-cron-input
title: Cron input
description: A schedule field people can read: cron or plain English in, the meaning in words and the next runs out, with clock changes flagged.

cavemio.accessibility:
- Five-field Unix cron: minute, hour, day, month, weekday, with names (MON, JAN), lists, ranges, steps, @daily-style shortcuts, L for the last day of the month, and FRI#2 or 5L for the nth or last weekday. 0 and 7 are Sunday. When both day and weekday are set, either one matching runs it, as in Unix cron; the sentence says so.
- English it reads: every N minutes or hours, from 9am to 5pm, weekdays, weekends, named days and ranges of them, the 1st and 15th, the last day, the second Tuesday, the last Friday, months, and times like 9, 9:30, 5pm, noon and midnight. What it can't say in cron ("9:30 and 17:00") it doesn't guess at.
- parseCron, describeCron, nextRuns and parseSchedule come from cron-parse.ts, which has no React in it, so a server or a worker can check and describe schedules the same way.
- The input has the field's label and is described by the sentence under it; errors mark it aria-invalid. The meaning is announced once typing pauses, never on each keystroke. Each run has its full text for screen readers; the rolling digits are hidden from them.
- Runs are worked out in the zone with Intl, day by day for up to six years, so a schedule that never fires (31 February) says so instead of hanging.
- Reduced motion: no glides, rolls or morphs; text and numbers change in place.
cavemio.previewNote: Interactive local fixture. Data and async results are simulated in the preview; the caller supplies application services.

props.name: value / defaultValue
props.description: "0 9 * * 1-5" · The schedule as cron. defaultValue may also be English ("every weekday at 9am"); the field starts with the words.

props.name: onValueChange
props.description: – · Each valid expression (tidied to single spaces, @macros expanded) and its parsed fields.

props.name: timeZone / defaultTimeZone
props.description: "UTC" · The IANA zone the schedule runs in; the runs are listed in it. Many schedulers (Vercel, GitHub Actions) only run in UTC.

props.name: timeZones
props.description: – · Zones to choose from. With two or more, the zone is a dropdown (Pill select) showing each zone's current offset.

props.name: onTimeZoneChange
props.description: – · Called when a zone is picked.

props.name: runs
props.description: 5 · How many upcoming runs to list; 0 hides them.

props.name: presets
props.description: CRON_PRESETS · Shortcuts above the field; [] hides them.

props.name: english
props.description: true · Read schedules typed in English.

props.name: name
props.description: – · Submits the expression with a form.

useCases.title: Scheduled jobs
useCases.description: Let people choose when a sync, an export or a backup runs.

useCases.title: Report emails
useCases.description: Weekly digests and reports that go out at the time each customer picks.

useCases.title: Workflow triggers
useCases.description: The “run on a schedule” step in automation tools and workflow builders.

useCases.title: Developer platforms
useCases.description: Cron settings for functions and workers, with the next runs shown before anything is saved.

features.title: Every part is named
features.description: Minute, hour, day, month and weekday sit under their parts, and the part you’re editing lights up.

features.title: It says it in words
features.description: “At 09:00, Monday to Friday”, updated with every keystroke.

features.title: It shows the next runs
features.description: The next five times it fires, in the schedule’s own time zone, before anything is saved.

features.title: It reads plain English
features.description: Type “every weekday at 9am” or “last friday of the month at 17:30” and Enter turns it into cron.

features.title: It points at mistakes
features.description: The wrong part turns red and says why: “The hour goes from 0 to 23, not 24.”

features.title: It catches clock changes
features.description: Runs that daylight saving skips or repeats are flagged, in London, New York or any other zone.

states.title: typing
states.description: The parts are spread with word spacing so their names (10.5px) fit under them. The name under the part your caret is in turns to the text colour and a 1px line glides to it (300ms); names follow their parts as the text changes (340ms).

states.title: meaning
states.description: The sentence under the field crossfades whole when it changes: the old one lifts out through a 4px blur in 180ms while the new one rises in (380ms, 60ms later).

states.title: runs
states.description: The next runs list day, time and how long until each. Hours and minutes roll in the direction they changed (700ms), dates and "in 3 h" morph letter by letter, and the list updates on each new minute.

states.title: english
states.description: Text with words that aren't cron names is read as English. The part names fold away (320ms), the sentence says what it understood and which cron it makes, and Enter or leaving the field morphs the words into the expression.

states.title: preset
states.description: A pill highlight slides to the preset that matches the expression (380ms). Picking one morphs the expression into the preset: characters both share glide, the rest rise in through a blur.

states.title: invalid
states.description: The part at fault gets a red line and a red name, the sentence says why ("The hour goes from 0 to 23, not 24.") and the runs stay at 45% opacity until the text is valid again. Escape morphs back to the last valid expression.

states.title: clocks
states.description: In a zone with daylight saving, a run at a time the clocks skip or repeat gets an amber mark and a line saying which.
